questions.prompt: John F. Kennedy was born in what Boston-area neighborhood?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Brookline. Not Dorchester. Not Boston proper. The Kennedys lived there until Joe started making real money.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Brookline. Everyone claims JFK for Boston, but he was actually born in Brookline. 83 Beals Street.

questions.prompt: Dorchester is the largest neighborhood in Boston by area. What fraction of Boston's total land does it represent?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: About one-sixth. Six square miles. More people, more history, more everything than the neighborhoods tourists visit.
questions.npcReactionWrong: One-sixth of Boston. Dorchester is bigger than people realize. This neighborhood has weight.

questions.prompt: What iconic Boston residential architecture style is most common in Dorchester?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Triple-deckers. Built for working families. Grandparents on one floor, parents on another, rental income from the third. That's how people survived.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Triple-deckers. Three floors, three families. You drive through Dorchester, you see the same house over and over.

questions.prompt: The Dorchester Heights Monument commemorates what military achievement?
choices: Washington's fortification that forced British evacuation
The first naval battle of the Revolution
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Washington put cannons up there. British looked up, saw they were outgunned, and left. March 17, 1776. That's why we celebrate Evacuation Day.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Washington's fortification. The British saw those cannons and evacuated Boston. No shots fired. Smart warfare.

questions.prompt: What Caribbean country's diaspora has one of its largest U.S. communities in Dorchester?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Cape Verde. Haiti too. Vietnam. This neighborhood has welcomed everyone. Sully used to say Dorchester was what America was supposed to be.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Cape Verde has one of its biggest American communities right here. Dorchester's been home to immigrants for generations.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What is the local nickname for Dorchester?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Dot. Locals don't say the full name. Just Dot.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Dot. That's what we call this neighborhood. Simple.

alternateQuestions.prompt: Dorchester was an independent town before being annexed by Boston in what year?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: 1870. Dorchester wasn't always part of Boston. When did the city swallow us up? 1870.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: 1870. We were our own town once. Then Boston came calling.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What famous bakery chain started near Dorchester in 1950?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Dunkin' Donuts. First store was in Quincy, but the company's roots are here. A coffee empire started in our backyard.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Dunkin'. Started nearby in 1950. Now it's everywhere. Boston runs on Dunkin'.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What major cultural event is held along Dorchester Avenue every summer?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Dot Day. Every June, this neighborhood throws its own parade. Been doing it for over a century.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Dorchester Day parade. Dot Day. This neighborhood celebrates itself every June.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What historic site in Dorchester is the oldest standing wooden building in Boston?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: The Blake House. Built around 1648. Before the Salem Witch Trials. Before anything. There's a house in Dorchester that's been standing for almost 400 years.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: The Blake House. Oldest standing wooden building in Boston. Been here since 1648. Think about that.
